prompt.context_jp: 三軒家万智も、背筋をまっすぐに伸ばして列の端に立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三軒家万智も、背筋___まっすぐに伸ばして列の端に立っていた。

feedback.correct_en: 伸ばす is a transitive verb taking a direct object; 背筋 is what she straightens, so を is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark 背筋 as a subject (as if the back straightened itself), and は would set it as topic, both wrong for this transitive action.

prompt.context_jp: バエ社員と言われて憤慨する三軒家。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___顔で 家を売ったことはありません！」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Machi uses to assert her stance.

feedback.correct_en: Machi declares her own stance as topic — 'As for me, I have never...'. は sets the speaker as topic/contrast against the implication that she uses her looks.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 私 as new information identifying who did it, which doesn't fit this emphatic denial.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who doesn't know.

prompt.context_jp: 課長への反論。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「課長 私の仕事___家を売ることです｡」

feedback.correct_en: 'My job' is the topic being defined — 'As for my job, it is to sell houses.' This A-は-B definition pattern uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new information ('it's my job that...'), which doesn't fit a definitional statement where 私の仕事 is already in focus.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の夢は医者になることです。
contrast_examples.en: My dream is to become a doctor.

prompt.context_jp: 課長が評価について説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「売り上げが上がらなくても 評価___下がりません｡」

feedback.correct_en: は marks 評価 as the contrastive topic — 'as for your evaluation (unlike sales), it won't go down'. The contrast with 売り上げ makes は natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 評価 as new information, but here it's being contrasted with 売り上げ, so contrastive は fits.

contrast_examples.jp: 値段は高いが、品質はいい。
contrast_examples.en: The price is high, but the quality is good.

prompt.context_jp: 契約が取れない日が続く足立の心境。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分でも理由が分からないまま、焦りだけ___胸の中に積もっていく。

feedback.correct_en: 焦りだけが describes new information — the sensation building up inside him. が introduces this emerging feeling as the subject of 積もる.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 焦りだけ a topic (already known), but this is the first time the narrative introduces this specific feeling piling up.

contrast_examples.en: The anxiety (that we knew about) disappeared.

prompt.context_jp: 誰が売ったのかをアピールする場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「3500万円で私___売りました！」

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is proudly identifying herself as the one who sold it — exhaustive-listing が ('it was I who sold it').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 私 a mere topic, losing the proud 'it was ME' nuance that fits the boast.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who did it!
As for me, I did it.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の決めゼリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私に売れない家___ありません！」

feedback.correct_en: With negation 「ありません」, は marks 'as for houses I can't sell — none exist.' This は-negation pattern is standard for emphatic denial.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply introduce the subject neutrally; the catchphrase gains its punch from topicalizing 売れない家 and then denying its existence.

prompt.context_jp: 朝倉の結婚について。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「朝倉___既婚者だよ｡」

feedback.correct_en: This is a statement about Asakura — 'As for Asakura, she's married.' A simple topic-comment definition uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is married?' as new information identification, but here Asakura is already the topic of discussion.

prompt.context_jp: 宇佐美が帰った後の朝倉の言葉。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「仕事に真剣に向き合うの___って 大変なことよ｡」

feedback.correct_en: のだって (= のでも/even...is) topicalizes with contrast — 'even seriously facing one's work is tough too.' This matches the source line.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just add new info without the 'too/even' contrastive nuance Asakura wants to convey against child-rearing.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の決まり文句。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私の仕事___家を売ることです｡」

feedback.correct_en: A定義 'A は B です' pattern — 私の仕事 is the topic being defined as 家を売ること.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'what is a job?' as if identifying which thing is her job among options; は is the standard definitional particle.

prompt.context_jp: 下の階の住人の文句。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「このマンション 造り___しっかりしてるといっても…」

feedback.correct_en: In descriptive subordinate clauses like 造りがしっかりしている (the construction is solid), the subject 造り is marked by が. This is a 'small-subject' structure within a larger topic (このマンション).
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't fit — しっかりしている is intransitive. に would mark location/target, not the subject of this adjective-like state.

contrast_examples.en: Elephants have long trunks (大主語/小主語).

prompt.context_jp: 物件紹介で近所の情報を伝える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「近所には大きな公園___あります｡」

feedback.correct_en: も adds the park to the list of nearby features already mentioned (daycare, supermarket). This 'also' nuance fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would contrast the park against those features; が would just introduce it neutrally, missing the additive feel.

prompt.context_jp: 下の階の住人が苦情を言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「家___仕事をしているもので…」

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action takes place — 'I do my work AT home.' The verb 仕事をする is an activity.
feedback.incorrect_en: に marks static location of existence (いる/ある), not the site of an action. を would require a transitive verb taking 家 as object.

prompt.context_jp: 上岡がプロポーズの計画を打ち明ける。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この家で 彼女___サプライズをしたいから…」

feedback.correct_en: に marks the recipient of the surprise — 'give a surprise TO her.' This is a goal/indirect object use of に.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make 彼女 the direct object of する, but サプライズ is already the object. で would mean 'by means of her,' which is wrong.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女にプレゼントをあげる。
彼女とサプライズをする。

prompt.context_jp: 白洲の決めゼリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私に取れない電話___ありません！」

feedback.correct_en: Mimicking Machi's 「売れない家はありません」, this uses topicalizing は with negation for the same emphatic 'none exists' effect.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a neutral existence statement, losing the parallel to Machi's catchphrase and the emphatic tone.

prompt.context_jp: 課長がプロジェクトを説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「輝く女性の 活躍の場を___ために 本社が鳴り物入りで始めた…企画」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 活躍の場.

feedback.correct_en: 活躍の場を広げる is the set collocation meaning 'expand opportunities to shine.' This is a standard business phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 開ける (open a hole/door) and 伸ばす (stretch/extend length) don't collocate with 活躍の場 in business discourse.

prompt.context_jp: 同僚に家探しを頼まなかった理由。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「気に入らなかった時に 変に気___使うの面倒だから｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the collocation 気を使う.

feedback.correct_en: 気を使う ('to be considerate/mindful') is a fixed collocation using を.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気になる/気がする exist but mean something different (feeling bothered / having a hunch). The verb 使う requires を.

prompt.context_jp: 課長が三軒家に休むよう命じる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「しっかり休養を___なさい｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 休養.

feedback.correct_en: 休養を取る ('take a rest/break') is the standard collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 休養を受ける/つける are not idiomatic. 受ける pairs with instruction/treatment; つける doesn't fit here.

prompt.context_jp: 課長が足立の過去の活躍を語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「足立クラブのマダムたち 手玉に___てたのに｡」

feedback.correct_en: 手玉に取る means 'manipulate / have (someone) wrapped around one's finger.' It's a fixed idiom with 取る.
feedback.incorrect_en: する/やる don't form the idiom; only 取る pairs with 手玉に.

contrast_examples.jp: 相手を手のひらで転がす

prompt.context_jp: 朝倉が三軒家を褒める。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「テーコー不動産の___にして 天才的不動産屋の三軒家さん…」

feedback.correct_en: 至宝 (しほう) means 'supreme treasure' — fitting for calling someone the jewel of the company.
feedback.incorrect_en: 至急 means 'urgent'; 至難 means 'extremely difficult.' Neither describes a prized person.

prompt.context_jp: 宇佐美が子育てママ層をターゲットに提案する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「子育て世代のママたちに ___ものがいいと思うんです｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'resonate with / stick with.'

feedback.correct_en: 刺さる (intransitive) is marketing slang for content that 'hits home' or 'resonates' with a target audience.
feedback.incorrect_en: 刺す is transitive ('to stab') and doesn't fit the に-pattern. 抜ける ('to come out') is the opposite meaning.

contrast_examples.en: an ad that resonates with young people

prompt.context_jp: 朝倉が男性心理を語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「女が仕事できると 自分の存在意義 ___ちゃうのよね｡」

feedback.correct_en: 疑う ('to doubt') fits — men start to doubt their own worth when women outperform them.
feedback.incorrect_en: 信じる (believe) is the opposite meaning; 叫ぶ (shout) is unrelated to 存在意義.

prompt.context_jp: 朝倉が三軒家を飲みに誘う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今夜 ___っと行かない？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the onomatopoeia meaning 'go have fun / let loose.'

feedback.correct_en: パーっと行く is a casual set phrase meaning 'go blow off steam / have a wild time.' It's idiomatic in invitations to drink or play.
feedback.incorrect_en: ホッと/スッと exist but mean 'relieved' / 'swiftly'; they don't fit the 'let's go party' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 課長が三軒家に業務指示を出す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for a 課長 giving a workplace instruction?

choices.text: 三軒家君は 通常の営業をセーブして プロジェクトに参加してください｡
三軒家さん 普通の営業を減らして プロジェクトを参加して｡
三軒家、営業セーブしプロジェクトに参加しろ。

feedback.correct_en: A matches the chapter's register — 君 for a subordinate + 〜してください is natural polite-but-authoritative workplace Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses the wrong particle (プロジェクトを参加 should be プロジェクトに参加). C is overly blunt/military and wouldn't fit this 課長.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が本社の会議で自己紹介する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which self-introduction sounds most natural in a formal business meeting?

choices.text: 新宿営業所 売買仲介営業課チーフ 三軒家でございます｡
新宿営業所の三軒家だよ。よろしく。
三軒家です、新宿営業所でチーフをやっています今。

feedback.correct_en: A follows the standard business self-introduction order: affiliation → title → name → でございます. This matches Machi's crisp professional style.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is far too casual for a cross-department meeting. C's word order is jumbled and ends with an unnatural 今.

prompt.context_jp: 足立が丁寧に客に確認する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural keigo when gently confirming with a customer?

choices.text: お連れ様は 上岡様が家をお買いになろうとしていることは ご存じないのですか？
あなたの彼女は 上岡さんが家を買うの 知らないの？
お連れ様は 上岡様の家買う件を 知ってないんですか？

feedback.correct_en: A uses layered keigo properly: お連れ様, お買いになる (sonkeigo for the customer), ご存じない. This matches a realtor speaking to a client.
feedback.incorrect_en: B drops all honorifics — far too casual for a client. C mixes 知ってない (ungrammatical/colloquial) and awkward 件を phrasing.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が自分の方針を明言する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural and in-character for Machi's clipped professional style?

choices.text: お客様を分別することは 私は いたしません｡
お客を区別するのは 私しないの。
客を分けること私はやりませんよ。

feedback.correct_en: A uses お客様 + いたしません (humble form), with topic-は fronting the action for emphasis — exactly Machi's crisp formal declaration style.
feedback.incorrect_en: B drops honorifics and uses casual ending の — unprofessional. C's ending よ is too soft/casual for Machi's declarative pronouncements.

prompt.context_jp: 白洲が失恋後、強がって宣言する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural as a defiant personal declaration?

choices.text: 私 これからは仕事に生きるんで｡
私はこれからで仕事を生きるので。
これから私が仕事に生きるんです。

feedback.correct_en: A matches the chapter line — 仕事に生きる is the idiomatic 'live for work,' and 〜んで trails off with casual emphasis, fitting Shirasu's dramatic self-pity.
feedback.incorrect_en: B misuses particles (これからで, 仕事を生きる — both wrong). C puts 私が (identification), implying 'I'm the one who,' which doesn't fit a personal resolution.
